findings.issue_text: [BUG] The diff keeps the original `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` (only its body is modified) and then adds a second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`, so the class defines `downsize` twice and in Ruby the later definition silently replaces the earlier one. The 4-argument signature is dead code: any caller invoking OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, w, h) binds max_width into `dimensions` and max_height into `opts`, and optimize then evaluates `opts[:allow_animation]` on an Integer, raising TypeError ("no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer") at the `_animated` check; 5-argument calls raise ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments, 5 for 3..4). The body the diff just modified in the first definition is unreachable, so the edit is a no-op and the public model API's arity contract silently changed.

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop ignores the return value of OptimizedImage.downsize, which convert_with sets to false when the convert command exits non-zero (`return false if $?.exitstatus != 0`), and performs no size check after the loop before handing the tempfile to Upload.create_for. A permanently failing convert (corrupt image, missing ImageMagick delegate) is retried 5 identical times per upload and the original oversized file is then stored, so max_image_size_kb is not enforced; even with successful converts, five 80% passes cap total reduction at ~67%, so files larger than ~3x the limit (reachable via API multipart uploads, which bypass the 10MB client-side cap) are still stored oversized. Each attempt also runs convert synchronously inside the request, tying up a worker for up to 5 invocations on large images.

[BUG] The client-side upload size check is changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to the hardcoded constant 10*1024, so the browser no longer enforces the configured limit at all. When an admin raises max_image_size_kb above 10240 KB, the web UI rejects files the server would accept (the server's downsize threshold is the setting) and the alert always claims the maximum is 10240 KB; when the setting is 0 — which previously blocked every upload client-side — uploads up to 10MB now pass, and the server's downsize guard (`SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb > 0`) skips reduction in exactly that case, storing the file at full size.

[ADVISORY] The API URL download cap is changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded 10.megabytes, decoupling it from the same setting that drives the downsize threshold two lines below. When max_image_size_kb is configured above 10240 KB, URL-sourced images larger than 10MB abort inside FileHelper.download, `rescue nil` yields a nil tempfile, and the later `tempfile.size` raises NoMethodError that the outer rescue converts into a generic upload failure — so URL-based uploads can never reach the downsize loop for limits above 10MB, while multipart uploads of the same files can.

[ADVISORY] The 413 error handler now reports a hardcoded 10240 KB limit instead of reading Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb. A 413 is produced by the web server's client_max_body_size, which is configured independently of both the old setting and this new constant, so users hitting the real server limit are shown a maximum that matches neither their site configuration nor necessarily the proxy's actual body-size limit.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds the downsize loop in create_upload and the OptimizedImage downsize/optimize signature refactor without any accompanying spec changes. The new behavior — the threshold comparison against SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, the 5-attempt cap, the FileHelper.is_image? gate, in-place mutation of the tempfile, and the reworked downsize/optimize arities — has no test coverage in this change; a regression such as an inverted size comparison or a wrong attempt count would silently store oversized or over-shrunk uploads with nothing to catch it.

[BUG] The diff leaves two competing `def self.downsize` definitions in the same class body — the modified 4-arg `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` version and the newly added 3-arg `(from, to, dimensions, opts)` version — and Ruby's last-definition-wins semantics silently make the 4-arg version dead code. Any caller still using the pre-existing 4-arg signature (including plugins) now binds the Integer height into `opts`, so `optimize` raises TypeError (no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer) at `opts[:allow_animation]` (ArgumentError for 5-arg calls); meanwhile the body the author edited at the first definition never executes, so the signature migration is silently incomplete.

[BUG] Hardcoding `10 * 1024` into the shared client-side size check replaces the per-type `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` gate for every upload type, not just images — the sibling flag `max_attachment_size_kb` is dropped from the path with no replacement. Attachments between the admin-configured `max_attachment_size_kb` and 10MB now pass the client check and, since the shown `create_upload` path performs no server-side size validation (oversize rejection relied on the client gate plus the web server's 413), are stored at full size — silently bypassing the configured limit; conversely, admins who raised `max_image_size_kb` above 10240 now get images between 10MB and their configured limit rejected with a message claiming the max is 10240 KB.

[BUG] The new downsize call passes an extensionless tempfile path (Rack multipart `RackMultipart*` files, or `Tempfile.new("discourse-upload-#{type}")` on the URL branch), so the `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` guard in `OptimizedImage.optimize` can never select the `*_animated` instructions on this path. Animated GIFs larger than `max_image_size_kb` are downsized with the non-animated convert instructions (no `-coalesce`), which resizes each partial frame independently and corrupts/strips the animation of the stored original — and the `SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` value the code dutifully passes has no effect on the outcome.

[BUG] The 5-attempt loop exits while `tempfile.size` can still exceed `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, so the acceptance criterion stated in the comment added directly above it ('will be automatically reduced to allowed size') is not guaranteed. Each pass shrinks linear dimensions to 80% (~36% of file size), so five passes leave roughly 11% of the original: a 10MB upload with `max_image_size_kb` at 1024 still lands at ~1.1MB, and `Upload.create_for` then stores the oversized image with no rejection, warning, or log entry.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds behavior-bearing logic — the downsize loop and the rewritten `OptimizedImage.resize`/`downsize`/`optimize` dispatch — without touching any spec or test file (no spec/**, test/**, or *.spec.* path appears in the diff), and no assertion verifies that an oversized upload lands at or below `max_image_size_kb`. A regression in the loop (unit mismatch, non-termination, or the duplicate-definition shadowing in optimized_image.rb) or in the new 3-arg downsize instruction building ships unverified; the repo's existing uploads/optimized-image specs predate this code and assert nothing about downsizing.

[ADVISORY] The loop ignores `OptimizedImage.downsize`'s return value (`convert_with` returns false on non-zero exit), so a persistently failing convert is re-run on the identical unchanged file until attempts are exhausted. A corrupt or unconvertible image costs up to five full ImageMagick decode/encode passes on a multi-megabyte file inside the request thread before the oversized original is stored silently, with no log line explaining why downsizing never happened.

[BUG] Hardcoding `FileHelper.download`'s cap at `10.megabytes` silently regresses API URL-pulls for sites that configured `max_image_size_kb` above 10240. On such sites, images between 10MB and the configured limit that previously downloaded and uploaded successfully now hit the download cap, get `rescue nil`'d to a nil tempfile, and crash `create_upload` with NoMethodError on `tempfile.size` (500) — the admin setting is dead in this path with no migration note.

[ADVISORY] The 413 handler now always reports `max_size_kb: 10240` regardless of the configured per-type limits or the web server's actual `client_max_body_size` that produced the 413. A user whose 3MB attachment is rejected because `max_attachment_size_kb` is 1024 (or because nginx is set lower) is told the limit is 10240 KB and hunts for a nonexistent 10MB cap.

[ADVISORY] The 10MB cap is now hand-maintained as three independent constants — `10 * 1024` at utilities.js:182, `10 * 1024` at utilities.js:246, and `10.megabytes` at uploads_controller.rb:55 — with no shared source of truth or site setting behind them. The next change to the cap must find all three sites; missing one reintroduces exactly the client/server limit skew this change creates (client gate, 413 message, and server download cap drifting apart).

[BUG] The client-side upload size gate replaces the per-type site setting lookup ('max_' + type + '_size_kb') with a hardcoded 10MB constant that is applied to every upload type, not just images. Sites configured above 10MB now reject files between 10MB and their configured limit that they previously accepted, while sites configured below 10MB let non-image files up to 10MB past this gate even though the new server-side downsizing explicitly excludes them (gated on FileHelper.is_image?), so the admin's per-type size policy is no longer what the client enforces; a max_image_size_kb of 0 is likewise still capped at 10MB client-side.

[BUG] The 413 (entity too large) handler now reports a hardcoded 10240 KB as the maximum size instead of any configured setting. Users whose uploads are rejected by the web server are told a limit that matches no configuration; because the client gate was simultaneously raised to 10MB, files between the real server cap and 10MB now reach the server and fail with this wrong message, whereas previously the client gate rejected them earlier with the configured limit.

[BUG] The API URL-download size cap is hardcoded to 10.megabytes, decoupling it from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb which previously governed it. Admins with max_image_size_kb above 10MB lose API URL uploads of images between 10MB and their configured limit (FileHelper.download fails and returns nil), while admins with lower limits get an unconfigurable 10MB fetch ceiling; the effective download cap for URL fetches is no longer controlled by any setting.

[BUG] The downsizing loop gives up after 5 attempts and ignores OptimizedImage.downsize's false return on convert failure, then unconditionally hands the still-oversized tempfile to Upload.create_for. Five 80% passes shrink pixel area to only ~11% of the original, so e.g. a ~10MB upload against a 1MB max_image_size_kb lands around 1.1MB and is stored over the configured limit with no error to the user; if any convert invocation fails (convert_with returns false on non-zero exit, which the loop discards), the original oversized file is stored untouched — the invariant stated in the new comment ('automatically reduced to allowed size') is not enforced.

[ADVISORY] The 10MB upload ceiling is hand-duplicated as '10 * 1024' in two places in utilities.js and as '10.megabytes' in uploads_controller.rb with no shared constant, setting, or single source of truth. Any future change to the ceiling must be replicated across three sites in two languages; a missed site leaves client acceptance and server handling inconsistent (e.g., client allowing 20MB while the server downloads only 10MB), and operators have no single knob to tune the ceiling.

[ADVISORY] The new downsizing loop and the OptimizedImage.downsize/optimize signature refactor ship with no test coverage anywhere in this diff. The 5-attempt cap, the is_image?/max_image_size_kb gating, and the exit path that uploads a still-oversized file are unverified, so a regression in the loop (e.g., downsize silently failing on every pass) ships over-limit uploads to production unnoticed.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedImage's public model API is reshaped — downsize drops from 5 to 4 parameters with a new third-argument semantic (geometry string instead of max_width), optimize's width/height pair merges into one dimensions string, and the dimensions helper is deleted — with no compatibility shim and no call sites updated in this diff other than the new controller call. An out-of-tree caller still using downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) binds the height integer to the opts parameter and crashes with TypeError (Integer#[] called with a Symbol) inside optimize at the opts[:allow_animation] check.

[BUG] The downsize gate keys on FileHelper.is_image?(filename), which is extension-based, so URL-fetched images whose filename lacks a recognized image extension skip the downsizing loop entirely. Pre-change the download cap itself bounded these files at max_image_size_kb; post-change an API image upload from an extension-less URL (common with signed/CDN URLs) is bounded only by the new hardcoded 10MB download cap and stored at up to 10MB regardless of the admin's configured limit.

[BUG] self.downsize is defined twice in the same class body (4-arg `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 146 and 3-arg `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 150); Ruby dispatches to the last definition, so the retained 4-arg signature is dead code. Any caller invoking the 4-arg form binds dimensions=max_width and opts=max_height (an Integer), raising TypeError ('no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer') at `opts[:allow_animation]` in optimize — or ArgumentError with 5 args — so the compatibility signature this diff deliberately keeps and modifies does not exist at runtime, and every caller of it breaks.

[BUG] The downsize call passes an extensionless Rack tempfile path, but optimize selects `downsize_instructions_animated` only when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, so the animated branch can never be taken for uploaded files even though the caller explicitly passes `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails`. Animated GIFs over max_image_size_kb are always downsized through the non-animated instruction path, losing the coalesce/deconstruct handling that variant exists to provide — corrupted animation frames for exactly the oversized uploads this feature targets (FileHelper.download tempfiles are extensionless too, so the API URL path has the same defect).

[BUG] Client-side upload validation no longer reads any site setting: maxSizeKB is hardcoded to 10*1024 here and in the 413 handler (line 246), replacing the `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` / `max_image_size_kb` lookup. For any site whose configured limit differs from 10240 KB the client now enforces a limit no admin set: sites with max_image_size_kb above 10MB reject uploads the server would accept, max_image_size_kb=0 (which previously blocked image uploads client-side entirely) now accepts them, and both error messages report a fictitious 10240 KB — max_image_size_kb silently changes meaning from reject-threshold to downsize target with no admin-facing update.

[ADVISORY] The 10MB upload cap now exists as three independent hand-maintained literals — `10 * 1024` (utilities.js:182), `10 * 1024` (utilities.js:246), and `10.megabytes` (here) — with no shared constant or site setting as a single source of truth. The next adjustment to the cap edits one copy and silently diverges the other two, producing client/server disagreement over what is allowed (client rejects what the server accepts or vice versa); a named constant or new site setting would leave exactly one place to update.

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop is best-effort while the comment promises 'automatically reduced to allowed size': 5 passes at 80% shrink to at best ~33% of the original (0.8^5), and the loop ignores `convert_with`'s false return (ImageMagick output is discarded to /dev/null). An image still over max_image_size_kb after 5 passes (10MB in with a 1MB limit lands at ~3.3MB) or any image whose conversion fails (corrupt file, missing binary) is stored oversized with no error or warning, so the admin's configured cap is silently violated and nobody learns the downsizing did not happen.

[ADVISORY] Up to five synchronous ImageMagick decode/encode passes now run inside the uploads request before Upload.create_for, and on the multipart path there is no server-side size check — the 10.megabytes literal guards only the API URL-download branch. Large uploads tie up a web worker for seconds per request and can hit reverse-proxy timeouts under concurrent load; on the multipart path the loop's input size is bounded only by the web server's body limit, so an oversized POST triggers five full convert passes on it in-request.

[ADVISORY] The new downsize loop — branching on is_image?, size comparisons, an attempt budget, and an in-place file rewrite whose result is consumed by Upload.create_for — ships with no test anywhere in this diff. A regression such as an inverted size comparison, a non-shrinking convert invocation, or a broken attempt counter would silently store oversized or corrupted uploads with no failing spec to catch it.

[BUG] OptimizedImage.downsize still has the signature downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) — this diff only rewrites its body to interpolate those two positional parameters — so the new call downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, '80%', allow_animation: ...) binds the trailing options hash to max_height, producing the geometry string '80%x{:allow_animation=>true}' and an empty opts hash. Every downsize iteration invokes ImageMagick with a malformed geometry and fails; convert_with returns false on non-zero exit (visible in this diff) and the controller ignores the return value, so after 5 futile attempts the loop exits and Upload.create_for receives the original, still-oversized tempfile — the feature never downsizes anything, and because the same diff raises the client-side limit to a hardcoded 10MB, large images are accepted and handed to upload at full size regardless of max_image_size_kb; the allow_animation option is also swallowed into the geometry string, leaving the animated-GIF branch unreachable from this call.

[BUG] The client-side upload guard is changed from the per-type site setting Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] to a hardcoded 10MB, dropping admin configuration for every upload type rather than only relaxing it for downsizable images. Attachments up to 10MB now pass the client check regardless of max_attachment_size_kb, and the server-side path added in this diff downsizes only files matching FileHelper.is_image?, so nothing in the changed code enforces the configured attachment limit — a silent policy change beyond the stated 'automatically downsize large images' objective.

[BUG] The downsizing loop never checks OptimizedImage.downsize's return value — convert_with returns false when the convert run fails — and exits after 5 attempts without verifying the file reached max_image_size_kb before unconditionally calling Upload.create_for. When downsizing fails or five 80% shrinks are insufficient (a 10MB image against a 1MB limit needs about 6 iterations), the oversized image proceeds to upload with no error, log, or user feedback — silently inverting the pre-diff behavior of rejecting oversized files and defeating the limit the feature promises to enforce.

[BUG] The API URL-download cap is changed from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes to a hardcoded 10.megabytes for downloads of every upload type. Attachment fetches via the API URL path are now permitted up to 10MB regardless of configured limits and the cap can no longer be tuned without a deploy; conversely, an admin who raises max_image_size_kb above 10MB gets URL downloads of those images aborted (swallowed by rescue nil) even though the new downsizing loop is supposed to accept them.

[BUG] The 413 handler now reports a hardcoded '10 MB' instead of Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb, decoupling the user-facing message from every configured limit. When the web server rejects an upload (client_max_body_size is configured independently of Discourse), users are told the limit is 10 MB even when the real limit differs, so retries sized by the message fail again.

[BUG] The new SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb > 0 guard inverts the meaning of a 0 value: before this diff the client rejected every non-empty file when the setting was 0 (fileSizeKB > 0), now 0 skips downsizing while the hardcoded 10MB client limit admits the image. An admin relying on max_image_size_kb = 0 to block image uploads now gets images up to 10MB accepted and created with no downsizing at all.

[ADVISORY] The 10MB upload cap is now hand-maintained as a literal in three places across two languages (utilities.js lines 182 and 246, uploads_controller.rb line 55) where a single site setting previously drove all of them. The next limit change requires synchronized edits in client JS and server Ruby and will silently drift (the two JS copies already differ only in their comment spelling), and nothing ties the constant to the web server's client_max_body_size that actually produces the 413s.

[ADVISORY] The downsizing loop — new behavior-bearing logic with an attempt cap, in-place file rewrite, and size re-check — ships with no test anywhere in this diff. A regression that makes downsize a no-op or misbinds its arguments (as in the signature finding) reproduces the silent oversized-upload failure with nothing to catch it, and the 5-attempt cap and the max_image_size_kb=0 behavior are likewise unverified.

[BUG] The new downsize gate validates the upload only by filename extension (FileHelper.is_image?(filename)) and byte size, never the content, so arbitrary non-image bytes named *.png/*.jpg are handed to ImageMagick convert (shell-executed via OptimizedImage.convert_with's backticks) for up to 5 passes per upload request. Any authenticated user can upload a file with an image extension containing arbitrary or crafted non-image bytes and force the server to parse those bytes with ImageMagick's parsers/delegates — a surface with a long history of memory-corruption and command-execution CVEs — five times per request, with no content validation anywhere in this path before the shell-out.

[BUG] The upload request path now synchronously runs ImageMagick decode/re-encode cycles up to 5 times on any upload exceeding SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, and the loop imposes no cap on the incoming tempfile size — the only size guards ahead of it are the client-side JS check (trivially bypassed by a direct POST) and the reverse proxy's body limit. An authenticated user scripting a handful of concurrent uploads of large or high-pixel-count (decompression-bomb) images forces sustained multi-second convert runs per request, exhausting web-process CPU and memory — a resource-amplification cost on the upload endpoint that did not exist before this change.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds a second OptimizedImage.downsize definition — downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) — below the existing 4-arg downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) whose body this same diff edits; Ruby keeps the later definition, so the edited 4-arg body is dead code. Maintainers editing the 4-arg downsize (e.g. changing the interpolation) see no runtime effect, and any caller still invoking the 4-arg form gets its arguments silently re-bound (max_width→dimensions, max_height→opts), producing malformed convert arguments or a NoMethodError instead of a resize.

[BUG] The diff adds a second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` while leaving the existing `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` in place a few lines above, so Ruby keeps only the last definition and the 4-arg body this same diff edits at line 146 is dead code. The effective public signature of OptimizedImage.downsize silently changed from (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) to (from, to, dimensions, opts): any existing caller or spec still using the documented 4-arg form crashes (ArgumentError when an opts hash is also passed, or TypeError from `opts[:allow_animation]` inside optimize when the height integer lands in opts), and any future fix applied to the shadowed body at line 146 silently has no effect.

[BUG] The downsize loop discards OptimizedImage.downsize's return value (convert_with returns false when the ImageMagick convert exits non-zero) and exits unconditionally after 5 attempts, so the loop can finish with tempfile.size still above SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb and the oversized file is handed to Upload.create_for anyway. When a convert run fails (corrupt/unsupported image, missing ImageMagick binary) the loop performs 5 no-op iterations and stores the original oversized file, silently bypassing the admin-configured limit this feature exists to enforce; even on the success path the 5-attempt cap lets inputs far above the limit (or deployments with a small max_image_size_kb) store files still over the setting, and nothing in this diff re-checks or rejects the result before it is stored.

[BUG] The `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` option is dead at this call site: optimize appends `_animated` only when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` (optimized_image.rb line 155), and `from` here is tempfile.path — a Rack multipart or `discourse-upload-#{type}` temp name that never ends in .GIF — so animated GIFs always take the non-animated instruction set. Animated GIFs are downsized without the animated (coalesce) instructions, so delta-frame GIFs come out with corrupted/misaligned frames, and the animated branch of the downsize path can never execute from the only caller that passes the option.

[ADVISORY] The client-side size check now hardcodes 10*1024 KB for every upload type, dropping the `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` lookup, and the 413 handler at lines 245-246 is changed to the same hardcoded constant instead of any setting. Admins' configured size limits are silently ignored client-side for all upload types (not just images), and both the too-large alert and the 413 error report a 10MB figure that no setting defines and that does not match the server-side downsize threshold, which still reads SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb — users are told limits the deployment doesn't actually enforce.

[ADVISORY] The API URL-download cap is hardcoded to 10.megabytes while the downsize threshold added a few lines below (line 66) still reads SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, leaving two independent constants governing the same upload path in one method. An admin who raises max_image_size_kb above 10240 KB to permit larger images gets silently capped at 10MB for API/URL uploads (FileHelper.download aborts larger fetches, leaving tempfile nil via the rescue), so the configured limit and the enforced cap drift apart with no single source of truth.

[ADVISORY] Downsizing by repeatedly re-encoding at 80% (up to 5 sequential convert runs on the same file) instead of computing a single resize to the target size compounds generational loss and multiplies synchronous ImageMagick work inside the upload request. An upload needing several steps is JPEG-re-encoded up to 5 times, producing compounding compression artifacts, and ties up the request thread for up to 5 sequential convert processes per oversized image; a single resize computed from tempfile.size versus the limit would make the attempt counter, the loop, and 4 of the 5 convert runs unnecessary with no generational loss.

[BUG] The diff updates the body of the existing downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) definition in place and then adds a second downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) definition immediately after it, so the class defines OptimizedImage.downsize twice and Ruby silently overrides the first definition with the second. The 5-argument form that is still printed in the source raises ArgumentError (given 5, expected 3..4) at runtime for any caller still using it (e.g. a plugin), and the retained first definition is dead code that misleads maintainers into editing a method that never executes; the signature refactor this diff performs is left half-applied.

[BUG] The downsize loop ignores the boolean returned by OptimizedImage.downsize (convert_with returns false on non-zero exit, per the kept code in optimized_image.rb), so a failing ImageMagick invocation leaves the tempfile untouched and the loop merely burns its 5 attempts on the unchanged file before falling through to Upload.create_for. On a server where convert fails (binary missing, ImageMagick policy/resource limits rejecting very large images — exactly this feature's target case — or corrupt input), the original oversized image is stored anyway, silently bypassing max_image_size_kb; the client-side check that used to reject such files was replaced by a hardcoded 10MB in this same diff, so nothing enforces the admin's limit.

[BUG] The new call passes tempfile.path as 'from', but OptimizedImage selects the _animated instructions only when from matches /\.GIF$/i (optimized_image.rb:155), and neither Rack multipart tempfiles nor Tempfile.new("discourse-upload-...") paths carry a file extension, so the animated branch can never fire for uploads processed here even though allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails is passed. Oversized animated GIFs are downsized by the static downsize_instructions path (single-frame convert), silently destroying the animation in the stored upload — the user's posted GIF loses all frames but the first with no error and no backup of the original, on sites that explicitly enabled animated thumbnails.

[BUG] The client-side size check is changed from the per-type lookup Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] to a hardcoded 10MB for every upload type routed through this function, not just images. Upload types whose configured limit is below 10MB (e.g. max_attachment_size_kb) are no longer rejected client-side; the only new server-side handling in this diff downsizes images exclusively (FileHelper.is_image? gate), so those files proceed to storage at full size with the admin's per-type limit unenforced, and the too-large error message now always claims 10MB regardless of configuration.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedImage.downsize is invoked with from == to (tempfile.path, tempfile.path), destructively overwriting the only server-side copy of the upload in place, up to five times, with no backup copy and no validation that the rewritten file is a readable image before Upload.create_for persists it. An abnormal termination mid-write (OOM kill, disk exhaustion during the convert) leaves a truncated file at the tempfile path and the user's original upload is unrecoverable; a convert that exits 0 with corrupt output is stored as-is with no detection.

[BUG] The loop caps reduction at 5 passes of 80% linear scale (~64% of pixel area per pass, so roughly a 9x size reduction total) and performs no post-loop size check, so uploads more than ~9x over max_image_size_kb exit the loop still over the limit and are stored oversized. With the 10MB client ceiling this diff introduces, any site running max_image_size_kb below ~1.1MB (e.g. 512 KB) stores near-10MB images at ~1MB — double or more the configured cap — instead of rejecting them, silently violating the 'reduced to allowed size' contract.

[ADVISORY] The API URL-download cap is hardcoded to 10.megabytes while the new downsize loop still reads SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, splitting the effective upload limit between hardcoded constants (this line plus the two 10MB literals in utilities.js) and the site setting. A site configured with max_image_size_kb above 10 MB regresses: URL-based API downloads of larger images now hit the hardcoded 10MB cap and fail (tempfile nil), and future limit changes must be hunted across three hardcoded literals plus the setting, which will drift.

[BUG] The diff adds a second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (lines 149-151) while keeping the modified 4-argument `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` (lines 145-147); Ruby silently replaces the earlier definition with the later one, so the updated 4-arg body is dead code and the pre-existing 4-argument contract is broken.
